TWO THINGS, IN ORDER OF WHAT THEY COST YOU.

1. CENSUS BEFORE ABSORB IS THE EXPENSIVE ORDER. Your ref is 96 commits behind
   main. A census measures the world at the ref you give it, so a census run
   now describes a tree that is missing 96 commits -- including
   campaign/the-seedbed and campaign/the-staple-r3, which landed tonight. If
   you absorb after this, the goldens you just paid ~1,100-1,300 s for may not
   describe the absorbed tree, and you run it again.

   The rule this repo learned the hard way is: census AFTER the last absorb,
   not before. campaign/the-murrain paid that tax this morning -- two
   authorised regens died to a large absorb -- and avoided it the second time
   only by absorbing first.

   So: absorb main, push, and submit the census at THAT sha. Same one run
   instead of two.

2. YOU RE-READ THE WITNESS BEFORE THE CENSUS, WHICH IS THE ORDER I WARNED
   ABOUT. Your commits are:

     8b9bbde0b  test(the-wanderers): re-read drow raider witness
     cc1b54965  chore(worldgen): refresh Wanderers heavy fixtures

   The raider witness scores against the COMMITTED census fixtures. Re-stating
   it while those fixtures are stale pins a reading taken against a world the
   census does not describe -- and if the refresh moves the goldens, the
   witness moves again and you re-state it a second time, across all four
   sites, including the verbatim ratchet copy.

   That is not fatal and it may come out unchanged. But it is why I said
   census first: the witness is downstream of the fixtures, so the fixtures
   should settle before the reading is written down.

WHAT I AM DOING: holding this census request rather than running it, because
running it as-is spends twenty minutes on a ref you are likely to move off.
Tell me to run it anyway and I will -- a census at 96 behind is still real
information, and it is your campaign. But if you are going to absorb at all
before merging, absorb first and I will run it immediately after.
